name: Song recreate
markdown:
# Song recreate

> From the author's earlier studio, cleaned for publication: private paths, ports and some lines were removed, so a step may read short and a screen it names may not exist here. Status in this studio: Untested.


## How to use it
1. Open **🎵 Music video** → **🎙 Song recreate**.
2. The song: a URL (long-form video / SoundCloud; the song library's safe import: allowlist, caps, provenance), a library
   song, an upload or a studio audio result.
3. Recreate it as: genre → subgenre (→ variation), lyrics (new lyrics on the same story and structure / the original
   words as a cover / instrumental), tempo (the original's or the style's), singer, language.
4. **🎙 Recreate the song**. The run downloads, analyses (tempo, sections, words heard by Whisper), shows what the song
   is about (the local LLM: summary, story, mood, voice, hook idea, themes), writes the new caption and lyrics, and
   waits for your OK (edit both). **Record it with Music 3**; **Another take** = a new seed; **Make a music video of it**
   hands the result to the music video maker.

## Rules
- The target caption is the subgenre's official Music 3 template (MINIMAX_MUSIC3: 94 % genre top-1 with AR 3.0); with
  tempo "original" only the template's bpm number changes. The original's story becomes the scenario line.
- New lyrics follow the original's section structure and line counts (2-8 per section, 40 max) and never reuse more
  than three consecutive words of an original line. Cover lyrics are the heard words on their sections.
- No artist, band or song name reaches Music 3: the style is the genre card.
- Studio-authored styles (the 15 dubstep ones in *Club, EDM, House & Trance*, 2026-10-17; see [music-video.md](music-video.md)) work like any other target, single or in a batch; the run notes (and a batch row's warnings) say "Studio-authored recipe, not an official Music 3 template, untested", and an *instrumental-led* variation with sung lyrics adds a note.
- A cover of someone else's song needs a cover / mechanical licence to release (informational: author).

## Batch song recreation (up to 10 songs in one run)
author request 2026-10-17: "also we should add batch song recreation". Every song is an ordinary Song recreate run (same safe import, same text guard, same
Music 3 path); the batch only changes the **order** the stages run in, and adds a view over all of them.

### How to use it
1. **🎙 Song recreate** tab, switch to **📚 Batch**.
2. **The songs**, up to 10: paste URLs one per line (a bullet or "1." in front is fine, a line with several URLs gives several songs; a line that is not a URL shows up refused),
   and/or add library songs, studio audio results and uploads. Each song has an optional **own settings** box (genre, subgenre, lyrics, tempo, singer, language); empty = the shared setting.
3. **Recreate them as**: the shared genre / subgenre / variation, lyrics mode (new / cover / instrumental), tempo, singer, language, and **Batch phases** (auto / on / off).
4. **Check the plan**: every row accepted or refused with its reason (host not on the import list, a playlist URL, the same song twice with the same settings, text the guard
   refuses, a kids version asked to be a cover ...), the batch-phases decision, and the **estimate**. **Start the batch** is enabled only when the plan can start.
5. Watch the songs. Each song is the normal run card: **Cancel / Retry**, **Drop** (leave it out of the batch), the review box, **Record it with Music 3**, **Another take** (new seed),
   **Make a music video of it**. **Approve all (n)...** is a button that asks once more ("Record all n songs exactly as written now?"); nothing approves by itself.
   The batch has **Pause**, **Resume** (after a pause, a cancel or a restart), **Retry failed** and **Cancel batch**.

### The order (batch phases on)
1. **Read** every song: the download (URL songs, the song library's own import) and the analysis (beats, sections, vocal separation + Whisper), CPU, one song after another.
2. **Understand** every song, then **write** every new caption and lyrics: the local writer LLM stays loaded for all of them (one writer load).
3. **Review**: every song stops for your OK (edit the caption and lyrics, then approve). A batch cannot skip this stop: the request has no "review off", a song set to skip is still held.
4. **Record**: the writer is dropped by the existing room logic (`llm_room.make_room_for_render`, idle content LLMs biggest first, only until Music 3 fits, never the  a local port unit),
   then the approved songs are recorded back to back, each through the ordinary generate path (text guard, output guard, the GPU turn, the 4 GB VRAM floor), one at a time.
   You can approve song 1 and let it record while you read song 2; recordings start only after phases 1-3 are finished for every song.

Never two GPU-heavy things at once: one coordinator thread does one stage at a time. **auto** = on from 3 songs (`batch_phases.py`'s rule); **off** = the batch is a queue of single
runs: one song start to finish (its review stop included), then the next; no writer drop. A song that fails (a bad URL, an unavailable video, the writer refusing its drafts) stops
nothing else; **Retry** puts it back at the stage it failed in.

### Time: measured history, estimate, measured run
The plan's step times come from **this box's own history**, not guesses (the earlier studio's songrecreate_timings.json, built read-only by
`tools/build_songrecreate_timings.py` from the studio job files and the song recreate runs; re-run it to refresh). Each number in the plan's fold-out says
**"measured, n=..., date"** or **"estimate, no samples on this box"**; a step falls back to its old guess only when it has no samples. Built 2026-10-17:

| Step | Number | Source |
|---|---|---|
| download (per URL song) | 10.6 s median (5.7-25.3) | **measured, n=88** finished `song:import` jobs (`render_s`; the wait for a CPU slot is not in it, and was often minutes) |
| analysis (vocal separation + Whisper, CPU) | 97 s median (97-163) | **measured, n=3** (thin: only three runs carry timings with the current pipeline) |
| understanding (writer, resident) | 5.2 s | **measured, n=1** (thin: one cover run sitting in review) |
| writing the new lyrics | 45 s | **estimate, no samples**: every real run on this box so far was a cover, none a rewrite |
| one Music 3 recording (load included) | 118 s median (49-194) | **measured, n=22** (5 with `render_s`, 17 by created to updated wall clock; `waited_s` was 0 for all) |
| a Music 3 load | 6.1 s median (2-20) | **measured, n=5**, mostly warm loads: a cold load after the writer swap is **not measured** |

The total is still a **projection** from those medians, so it is labelled "estimate" with "k of 7 step times measured". Batching saves **model-swap dead time** (one writer load
and one Music 3 load instead of one of each per song, about 47 s per extra song at the numbers above), **not render time**: every song still takes its own Music 3 recording. Your
review time and any wait for the GPU or a CPU slot are not in the numbers. While it runs the batch records the **measured** seconds per phase (and the Music 3 jobs' own
`render_s` / `load_s`), shown next to the estimate. Run one batched and one unbatched set of the same songs to turn the saving into a measurement.

### Rules (unchanged)
- No artist, band or song name reaches Music 3 (the style comes from the genre card; the source title is only ever given to the writer, which is told not to use names).
- New lyrics never reuse more than three consecutive words of an original line (the same writer prompt as one song). A cover is informational: releasing a cover of someone else's song needs a cover / mechanical licence (the plan and the song's card say so).

### State, restart and what does not happen
A batch is one JSON file (`<state>/songrecreate/batches/sb<12 hex>.json`) plus each song's run file. After a studio restart the batch shows **Interrupted** and its cut-off songs
**Interrupted**; **Resume** puts them back where they stopped (a song that was waiting for your OK goes back to waiting). **Nothing starts by itself on boot.** Only one batch works at a time
(starting another says so); a batch waiting for your OK does not block a new one.

### A single song queues behind a working batch (author 2026-10-17)
A run started from the One song tab (start, approve, another take, resume) while a batch is working is saved as **Waiting for the batch** (status `waiting`, visible in the One song tab, with
the text "waiting for the batch") and starts by itself, oldest first, when the batch **finishes, pauses, is cancelled or fails** (a batch that is only waiting for your OK is idle and does
not hold it). A waiting run can be cancelled, and Resume while a batch is working puts it back to waiting. The same lane works the other way round: a batch does not start a stage while a
single-song run is working, it waits ("waiting for a single-song run to finish"; Cancel or Pause ends the wait). After a restart a waiting run is **Interrupted**; it does not start by itself
(Resume starts it, or queues it again if a batch is working).

### Honesty
Wired and tested with fakes (import, analysis, LLM, Music 3 and the writer drop are all stand-ins); the batch UI is syntax- and helper-tested only. Nothing was recorded as a batch and no
download was made; the step times above are medians read from the studio's existing job history, not timed by the batch. Proof level: **recipe**. Like one song, the Music 3 recording itself is "untested on the GPU" in this tab's own words.
